source.title: On Data Scaling in Masked Image Modeling
source.authors: Zhenda Xie; Zheng Zhang; Yue Cao; Yutong Lin; Yixuan Wei; Qi Dai; Han Hu

record.tranche_reason: It measures pre-training loss and downstream performance using Pearson correlations, a different method for assessing downstream predictability than the original language-model scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper studies masked-image-modeling data scaling and reports training/validation losses and downstream results, but does not fit or test power laws, extrapolate from small runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its image data-scaling results are relevant to V5's setting but do not measure whether the same power-law form holds. The loss–downstream correlation results bear directly on V6. The paper also reports many scaling and fine-tuning accuracies; they are not rows here unless they measure the loss–downstream relationship. Table 7's extracted values are paired with overfit-status labels in the table, but this pairing conflicts with the prose description; this ambiguity is noted in the relevant rows.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (SimMIM masked-image pre-training of SwinV2 vision encoders), it reports how pre-training training and validation losses correlate with fine-tuning performance on five vision tasks. This bears on V6 (downstream predictability from pretraining loss). It is T3 rather than T2 because the system is a vision encoder, not a language model. No power laws are fitted, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MIM is data-scalable as well as model-scalable, provided training is long enough. Large models overfit on small data. Validation loss correlates strongly with fine-tuning performance across tasks and can proxy for model evaluation. Training-loss correlation changes sign around overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SimMIM masked-image reconstruction with SwinV2 image encoders and pixel regression losses, not autoregressive language-model pre-training or language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: The training-loss/fine-tuning relationship changes with overfitting status; validation-loss correlations remain negative across the reported tasks and groups.

fits_no_version.finding: MIM vision encoders overfit with small pre-training data. The benefit of more data appears only with longer training, and larger models saturate more slowly as data grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-scaling benefits in self-supervised image pre-training depend on training length and model size; data-limited large models overfit and lose downstream accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (venue stated in the record); the paper text identifies itself as a preprint.
record.problems: Table 7's group labels for training-loss correlations conflict with the prose description of which overfit group has positive versus negative correlations. The reported evidence is correlation rather than a predictive validation on held-out downstream outcomes, and does not address language models or power-law fits.
record.rows_left_out: No further rows from Table 7 were omitted. Other reported scaling losses and downstream scores were not extracted because they do not measure the loss-to-downstream-performance relationship tested here or a fitted power law.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, data or compute; and not language models.
Encoder depth/width not varied; authors list this as a limitation.
Image MIM loss vs data, model size and training length is reported only in curves and tables; no power-law form is fitted or tested.
No functional fit or held-out prediction of downstream scores. Correlation only. No language-model tasks.

missing.what: Downstream fine-tuning scores across model size, data fraction and training iterations, showing non-monotonic gains (larger or longer-trained models worse on small data)
Validation-loss vs fine-tuning linear-fit slopes differ markedly between overfit and non-overfit groups

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a vision-MIM setting, not language models. Evidence for V6 is Pearson correlations only; group sizes, significance and predictive validation are not reported. The prose in Section 3.3 swaps group/colour wording relative to the Figure 4 caption. Table 7's assignment (overfit = positive train-loss correlation) is physically plausible.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits for held-out language-model loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or large-run loss extrapolations.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal fit.
The paper notes that encoder depth and width were not studied as a data-scaling factor; it does not test whether architecture details have little effect at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies masked image modeling and data scaling, but does not test whether its losses follow the same power-law form as language-model losses.

Tests correlations between pre-training losses and fine-tuning performance on image tasks; does not test language-model downstream tasks or whether downstream performance improves predictably with model scale itself.
No comparison of fitted exponents, parameter-count conventions, fitting methods, or compute-optimal allocations.

relationships.condition: Image MIM, validation (held-out) pre-training loss, all five tasks, both overfit and non-overfit groups
relationships.reason: Validation-loss Pearson r is negative in every case, from -0.54 to -0.91 (r3, r4, r7, r8, r11, r12, r15, r16, r19, r20).
relationships.display_finding: Pearson correlations between validation loss and downstream performance were negative in every case, ranging from -0.54 to -0.91 across both overfit and non-overfit groups.

relationships.condition: Image MIM, training (non-held-out) loss, especially overfit models
relationships.reason: Train-loss correlation is positive for overfit models (r1, r5, r13, r17; r9 near zero) and weak for some non-overfit tasks (r6, r14, r18). Predictability therefore depends on which loss is used and on overfitting.
relationships.display_finding: Training-loss correlations were positive for most overfit models but near zero or weak in some comparisons.

relationships.condition: Image MIM, downstream accuracy vs model size or training length with small pre-training data (text-based, no rows)
relationships.reason: Per Tables 3 and 5, larger or longer-trained models do worse on small data (SwinV2-H 84.4 vs L 84.7 on IN1K 20%). Downstream performance does not improve monotonically with scale when data is the bottleneck.
relationships.display_finding: Larger or longer-trained models performed worse with little data, with SwinV2-H scoring 84.4 versus SwinV2-L's 84.7 on IN1K 20%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Validation loss across the five reported downstream tasks and both overfit-status groups
reader_labels.reason: Validation-loss correlations with fine-tuning performance are negative in every reported group, ranging from -0.54 to -0.91 (r3, r4, r7, r8, r11, r12, r15, r16, r19, r20). The authors also state validation loss has stronger linear correlation than training loss for all cases.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Training loss across overfit-status groups and downstream tasks
reader_labels.reason: Training-loss correlations vary by subgroup and task, including weak or opposite-direction values in Table 7; the table's subgroup labels also conflict with the prose description (r1-r2, r5-r6, r9-r10, r13-r14, r17-r18).
